items.answer: Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office must work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team to ensure onsite days overlap and office time is collaborative; most teams anchor on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average in MosaicOne rather than week by week, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem. Weeks containing a company holiday, approved PTO or approved travel reduce the requirement proportionally.

Next steps:
- Confirm your assigned hub office and team's specific onsite days with your manager

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

Retirement plan eligibility is different and shorter: an employee may begin contributing to the 401(k) plan from their first payroll run, with no waiting period at all.

Next steps:
- Confirm your hire date to calculate your specific coverage start date
- Review your benefits elections in MosaicOne Benefits within 30 days of eligibility

Mosaic Robotics will never ask an employee for their password, and no genuine internal request will ever ask for a payroll change, a payment redirection or a bulk personal-data extract over email alone. Requests of that shape are verified by a second channel before anyone acts on them, every time, without exception, regardless of who appears to have sent them.

Report suspected phishing by forwarding the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example. The security team answers every report, including the ones that turn out to be legitimate mail, and publishes a short monthly summary of what was seen.

Recommendation — not company policy: Do not reply to the message and do not act on the request. This matches the pattern of a phishing lure: an unexpected request from someone senior, urgency, and a request for sensitive data over email alone without a second verification channel.

Next steps:
- Forward the email to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example
- Delete the message
- Do not send the employee roster or any sensitive data

Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories. The allowance resets on 1 January and does not carry over. It is available to hybrid and fully remote employees; onsite employees may claim against it only where their manager has agreed a regular remote pattern in MosaicOne.

The allowance is intended for things that make a home workspace work: a desk, a chair, a lamp, a footrest, an adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, a small filing cabinet. Laptops, monitors, docks, keyboards, mice, headsets and webcams are not claimed against this allowance—they are issued as company assets under the Equipment & Asset Policy.

Next steps:
- Submit home office claims in MosaicOne Expenses
- Confirm your work arrangement qualifies you for the allowance with your manager if you are onsite

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent. The 16 weeks are the same whether the employee gave birth, did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Next steps:
- Confirm your eligibility (6 months of continuous service required)
- Contact People Operations to discuss timing and any splitting of leave into up to three blocks

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the cap cannot be met, the traveller books the most reasonable available option and notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed.

Next steps:
- Consult MosaicOne Travel for market-specific rates or exceptions

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins. The review determines whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure. The request is raised in MosaicOne alongside the manager approval and names the destination, the exact dates, the workspace address and a short description of the work the employee will perform while abroad.

A trip that exceeds 30 consecutive days also requires director approval rather than direct-manager approval. Manager approval, director approval and Tax & Legal approval are three separate records and all three must be present before departure.

Next steps:
- Submit Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne at least 21 calendar days before departure
- Obtain director approval (not just manager approval)
- Await Tax & Legal review outcome before finalizing travel plans

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more.

For a USD 3,000 expense report, the direct manager approves the spend, as the report total falls within the up to USD 2,500 threshold or the USD 2,501 to USD 10,000 threshold requiring director approval with Finance business partner review.

Next steps:
- Book flights through MosaicOne Travel at least 14 days before departure
- Obtain manager approval before booking the trip
- Retain itemised receipts for all expenses USD 25 and above
- Submit expense report in MosaicOne for approval routing

Security and acceptable-use training must be completed within 14 calendar days of the start date. This is the only training with a hard deadline shorter than 30 days because system access is granted on day one.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. An employee has 30 days from the end of the waiting period to make benefits elections in MosaicOne Benefits. An employee who makes no election within that window is enrolled in employee-only coverage on the standard medical plan by default.

Standard equipment is shipped to arrive at least 5 business days before the start date. For a new engineer, this includes a 14-inch developer laptop with 32 GB of memory, a power adapter, a headset, and a laptop bag. For remote hires, it also includes a monitor, keyboard, mouse and dock.

Recommendation — not company policy: Complete the full required training set — security and acceptable use, data protection and privacy, anti-harassment and respectful workplace, and anti-bribery and corruption — within 30 calendar days of your start date, even though security training has the tighter 14-day deadline.

Next steps:
- Complete security and acceptable-use training by day 14
- Make benefits elections within 30 days of your 90-day eligibility date (day 120 from hire)
- Confirm receipt and setup of your standard laptop and peripherals before day one

Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours. Response means a named human being contacting the person who raised the case, acknowledging what was raised, naming who owns it and describing what happens next.

Target resolution time for Severity 1 cases is as fast as the facts allow. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update. Updates continue at least every 10 business days until the case closes.

Escalation: The published policy does not specify a separate investigation timeline distinct from the overall response and resolution targets for Severity 1 cases. Contact People Operations for details on investigation procedures and timelines.

Next steps:
- Contact People Operations if you need clarification on investigation timelines for a specific case
- Reference your case number when inquiring about case progress

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

Unforeseeable absences — a sudden illness, a family emergency, a transport failure that makes work impossible — are never held to the notice requirement. The employee notifies their manager as early as they reasonably can, and the absence is entered in MosaicOne retroactively, against sick time where the reason was illness and against PTO otherwise.

Recommendation — not company policy: As of 2026-09-01, you have 13.5 remaining PTO days. You accrue 1.5 days per month and have accrued 13.5 days year-to-date with no usage or carryover. Your next accrual date is 2026-10-01. Note that 2026-12-22 and 2026-12-23 are blackout dates.

Next steps:
- Submit PTO requests in MosaicOne at least 5 business days before your intended absence, or 15 business days for absences of 6+ consecutive business days
- Contact your manager if you need to discuss coverage or have questions about your specific request

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice.

Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne. Verbal agreement, a message in chat and an email thread are all insufficient on their own.

As of 2026-09-01, your remaining PTO balance is 13.5 days, which covers the three days requested.

Recommendation — not company policy: Submit your request in MosaicOne now to meet the 5 business day advance notice requirement for the September 15–17 dates. Your manager must approve it in writing within the system before the absence can be recorded.

Next steps:
- Submit the PTO request in MosaicOne for September 15–17, 2026
- Ensure your direct manager approves the request in writing before the first day of absence

You have completed 45 months of continuous service as of 2026-09-01, exceeding the 12-month tenure requirement to work outside your home country.

Germany is an approved destination for temporary work abroad.

Your proposed stay from 3 November to 14 December 2026 is 42 consecutive calendar days, which exceeds the 30-day threshold and requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins, director approval (not just manager approval), and written manager approval at least 21 calendar days before departure.

The 42-day stay falls within the rolling 90-day annual limit for work outside your home country.

Work performed outside your home country must use a company-managed, full-disk-encrypted laptop with always-on VPN; personal devices may not be used.

Recommendation — not company policy: Notify IT Security of your Berlin destination at least 5 business days before departure so that conditional-access rules and travel-risk monitoring can be adjusted.

Escalation: You can proceed, but only after obtaining three separate approvals: written manager approval from Dana (your direct manager), director approval, and Tax & Legal review. File the Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne at least 21 calendar days before 3 November 2026, naming the destination, exact dates, workspace address, and a description of your work. Contact mobility@mosaicrobotics.example to coordinate the process.

Next steps:
- Raise the request in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country' with exact dates (3 November – 14 December 2026) and Berlin workspace address.
- File a Tax & Legal review request at least 21 calendar days before 3 November 2026.
- Obtain written manager approval from Dana and director approval before departure.
- Confirm with IT Security that your travel laptop is company-managed, encrypted, and on always-on VPN.
- Notify IT Security of your Berlin destination at least 5 business days before departure.

Your 90-day waiting period ends on 2026-11-13 (as of 2026-09-01). You will become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage on that date.
